results.title: The Impact of COVID-19 on Airfares—A Machine Learning ...
results.content: The impact of the COVID-19 policy shift is the deviation between the ML-predicted airfares for 2020 trained on pre-COVID-19 data and the actual prices in 2020. The prediction error of the ML model was neglectable over the whole observation period, revealing its suitability for predicting counterfactual control scenarios for the evaluation of universal policies. The prediction models were based on air carrier data from ICAO Data Plus and airfare data from Sabre Market Intelligence. The impact of the COVID-19 policy shift was calculated as the deviation in the ML predicted airfares trained on pre-COVID-19 data and the actual airfares in 2020. More importantly, this paper shows that multi-step prediction based on ML and walk-forward validation is a preferable framework to evaluate predicted counterfactual control scenarios. results.title: Forecasting air passenger numbers with a GVAR model
results.content: ## Annals of Tourism Research. # Forecasting air passenger numbers with a GVAR model. This study employs a GVAR model on air passenger forecasting. It jointly analyses the micro and macro perspectives of air passenger forecasting. The GVAR model achieves most accurate forecasts for several airports. This study employs a GVAR model on the passenger numbers of the top 20 busiest airports of the world and the Asia-Pacific and Latin America-Caribbean regions. In terms of ex-ante forecast accuracy, the GVAR model performs best for several airports – yet not for the entirety of airports – compared to four benchmarks for horizons one and three quarters ahead.
